name.text: Naming a transformation from its matrix

questiontext.text:
Each matrix below represents one transformation. Choose its name.

Hint: where do (1, 0) and (0, 1) go?

(a) \({@M1@}\) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]
(b) \({@M2@}\) [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]
(c) \({@M3@}\) [[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prt3]]
(d) \({@M4@}\) [[input:ans4]] [[validation:ans4]] [[feedback:prt4]]

generalfeedback.text:
Read the columns: the first column of a matrix is where (1, 0) goes and the second is where (0, 1) goes. Sketch the unit square and its image, then name the transformation.

  • (a) [[if test="is(K1=\"rx\")"]]\((1,\,0)\) stays where it is and \((0,\,1)\) goes to \((0,\,-1)\): only the y-coordinate changes sign, so points flip across the x-axis. It is the reflection in the x-axis.[[/if]][[if test="is(K1=\"ry\")"]]\((1,\,0)\) goes to \((-1,\,0)\) and \((0,\,1)\) stays where it is: only the x-coordinate changes sign, so points flip across the y-axis. It is the reflection in the y-axis.[[/if]][[if test="is(K1=\"ryx\")"]]\((1,\,0)\) goes to \((0,\,1)\) and \((0,\,1)\) goes to \((1,\,0)\): the coordinates swap without changing sign, \((x,\,y)\) to \((y,\,x)\). It is the reflection in the line \(y = x\).[[/if]][[if test="is(K1=\"rmyx\")"]]\((1,\,0)\) goes to \((0,\,-1)\) and \((0,\,1)\) goes to \((-1,\,0)\): the coordinates swap and both change sign, \((x,\,y)\) to \((-y,\,-x)\). It is the reflection in the line \(y = -x\).[[/if]][[if test="is(K1=\"r90\")"]]\((1,\,0)\) goes to \((0,\,1)\) and \((0,\,1)\) goes to \((-1,\,0)\): a quarter turn anticlockwise about O.[[/if]][[if test="is(K1=\"r180\")"]]\((1,\,0)\) goes to \((-1,\,0)\) and \((0,\,1)\) goes to \((0,\,-1)\): both coordinates change sign but do not swap, \((x,\,y)\) to \((-x,\,-y)\). That is a half turn about O.[[/if]][[if test="is(K1=\"r270\")"]]\((1,\,0)\) goes to \((0,\,-1)\) and \((0,\,1)\) goes to \((1,\,0)\): a quarter turn clockwise about O.[[/if]]

questiondescription.text:
Matrices and Transformations: naming a transformation from its matrix

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.1: Name the reflection or rotation about O represented by each of four standard matrices.

Core

This question is adapted from Chapter 14, Exercise B, Question 1 of School Mathematics Project, SMP Book 5 (Metric), ed. P. G. Bowie, Cambridge University Press, 1969: standard matrices only, named from a fixed list with named feedback for the partner transformation, randomised.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text:
You chose [[if test="is(ck=\"id\")"]]the identity, which leaves (1, 0) and (0, 1) where they are[[else]]the [[if test="is(ck=\"rx\")"]]reflection in the x-axis[[/if]][[if test="is(ck=\"ry\")"]]reflection in the y-axis[[/if]][[if test="is(ck=\"ryx\")"]]reflection in the line \(y = x\)[[/if]][[if test="is(ck=\"rmyx\")"]]reflection in the line \(y = -x\)[[/if]][[if test="is(ck=\"r90\")"]]rotation of \(90^\circ\) anticlockwise about O[[/if]][[if test="is(ck=\"r180\")"]]rotation of \(180^\circ\) about O[[/if]][[if test="is(ck=\"r270\")"]]rotation of \(90^\circ\) clockwise about O[[/if]], which sends (1, 0) to \(({@Cm[1,1]@},\,{@Cm[2,1]@})\) and (0, 1) to \(({@Cm[1,2]@},\,{@Cm[2,2]@})\)[[/if]]. This matrix sends (1, 0) to \(({@M1[1,1]@},\,{@M1[2,1]@})\) and (0, 1) to \(({@M1[1,2]@},\,{@M1[2,2]@})\): its columns.

[[if test="is(K1=\"rx\")"]]Both reflections in an axis keep one of \((1,\,0)\) and \((0,\,1)\) where it is. The one that stays lies on the mirror line.[[/if]][[if test="is(K1=\"ry\")"]]Both reflections in an axis keep one of \((1,\,0)\) and \((0,\,1)\) where it is. The one that stays lies on the mirror line.[[/if]][[if test="is(K1=\"ryx\")"]]Both reflections in a diagonal line swap the coordinates. Check the signs.[[/if]][[if test="is(K1=\"rmyx\")"]]Both reflections in a diagonal line swap the coordinates. Check the signs.[[/if]][[if test="is(K1=\"r90\")"]]Both are quarter turns about O. Anticlockwise takes \((1,\,0)\) up to \((0,\,1)\); clockwise takes it down to \((0,\,-1)\).[[/if]][[if test="is(K1=\"r180\")"]]Both change the signs of the coordinates. The reflection in \(y = -x\) also swaps them; check whether this matrix does.[[/if]][[if test="is(K1=\"r270\")"]]Both are quarter turns about O. Anticlockwise takes \((1,\,0)\) up to \((0,\,1)\); clockwise takes it down to \((0,\,-1)\).[[/if]]
